# Setting the Stage {#sec-setting-the-stage}

The following video by Nicolas Vandeput served as the inspiration for *Pythia’s Advice*. It highlights the importance of establishing a statistical benchmark for forecasting accuracy — one that is both transparent and independent of commercial software or human bias.

Building on this idea, *Pythia’s Advice* aims to generate forecasts using free, open-source, state-of-the-art statistical methods from the [`fable`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/fable/index.html) package developed by
Professor [Rob J Hyndman](https://robjhyndman.com/) of the Monash University in Melbourne.

These forecasts are designed to require minimal effort, cost, and human intervention, providing a robust and objective reference point. By comparing these statistical forecasts to those produced by the business, we can assess the **Forecast Value Added (FVA)** — a measure of how much value, if any, human-driven forecasting processes bring beyond what data alone can achieve.


> Don't compare your forecasting accuracy to industry benchmarks. 

</BR>

<figure>

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/embed/0f42bR_JF78 title="Don't compare your forecasting accuracy to industry benchmarks." >}}

<blockquote>

Don't compare your forecasting accuracy to industry benchmarks.\
They're irrelevant.

Instead, compare your forecasting accuracy against simple statistical benchmarks such as moving averages.\
Moving averages are a fair benchmark: they will deliver higher (or lower) accuracy depending on the product, period, and market.\
That's perfect.\
Also, they're free.

Industry benchmarks are expensive and they don't compare apples to apples.\
Your competitors are present in different markets, with different clients and product portfolios. So, it's normal if they achieve different levels of accuracy.\
Moreover, you're unsure of how accuracy is tracked by your competitors (granularity, horizon, and metrics – I hope it's not MAPE).

</blockquote>

<figcaption>text and insight by <cite>Nicolas Vandeput</cite> (<a href="https://www.supchains.com">supchains.com</a>)</figcaption>

</figure>
